risks.title: Cyberattack by nation-state actor
risks.score_rationale: The risk is mentioned in the first section of risk factors with strong language (nation-state threat actor, long-term persistent access). The exfiltration of BIG-IP source code and undisclosed vulnerabilities represents a potential existential threat to customer trust. The text indicates expected impacts on sales cycles and operating margin in 2026, reinforcing severity. The cybersecurity category is highly critical in the IT sector.

risks.title: Sales cycle disruption post-cyberincident
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly states an anticipation of near-term disruption to our sales cycles with a stronger impact at the beginning of fiscal year 2026. The language is clear and forward-looking, showing a direct consequence of the cyberincident. Although temporary, this affects growth and competitiveness against rivals. The competition category is heavily weighted here as the risk involves potential loss of market share or deals.

risks.title: Dependence on macroeconomic demand
risks.score_rationale: The risk is repeated across multiple sections with significant language (uncertain economic conditions, inflation, tariffs, higher interest rates). It relates to customer demand stability, particularly sensitive for Fortune 1000 enterprises. Compared to the prior year, the tone is more cautious, indicating a perceived worsening of the risk. The macro category is critical for enterprise IT solution sales.

risks.title: Revenue concentration on two distributors
risks.score_rationale: Two distributors alone account for 33.3% of revenues (15.8% and 17.5%). The risk is stable compared to the prior year, but dependency remains high. The text shows no notable improvement or diversification. Losing a single partner would have a significant impact on distribution. The competition category is selected as it affects negotiation power and resilience against competitors.

risks.title: Evolution of software consumption models
risks.score_rationale: The shift from perpetual licenses to subscription and SaaS is mentioned as a factor that may affect the timing and classification of revenues. The language is cautious but recurring, particularly in the Critical Accounting Estimates section. This risk is stable but structural, tied to digital transformation. The technology category is moderately weighted, but critical for revenue predictability.

risks.title: Pressure on product margins
risks.score_rationale: Product gross margin declined from 28.1% in 2023 to 22.4% in 2025, despite partial improvement in 2025. The text cites factors such as hardware costs, component price increases, and supply chain constraints. Although partially offset by a more favorable mix, margin pressure persists. The risk is stable but significant for profitability. The capital category reflects the impact on cash generation.

risks.title: Increased expenses related to cyberincident
risks.score_rationale: The company expects to incur additional professional and other expenses in 2026 related to incident response. While deemed not material at this stage, they are anticipated to recur in the following fiscal year. The language is measured but forward-looking. The capital category is relevant as it affects operating cash flow. The risk is new but of moderate intensity.
